key_insight: The paper proves wavenumber-explicit stability and preasymptotic error bounds for a UPML-truncated finite element model of 2D Helmholtz obstacle scattering, with inf-sup stability scaling like O(k^-1).
engineering_relevance: This gives a rigorous basis for using UPML CIP-FEM to simulate high-frequency wave scattering with predictable accuracy and controlled truncation error.
method: Derive direct estimates for the stretched Green kernel under Cartesian complex coordinate stretching
Prove explicit stability for the truncated UPML problem and exponential decay of PML truncation error
Combine piecewise H^(1+s) regularity with CIP-FEM to obtain wavenumber-explicit preasymptotic FEM error estimates
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical stability/error analysis and numerical experiments that confirm the predictions and show effectiveness in the high-frequency regime.
watch_item: The analysis relies on fractional regularity across PML interfaces and corner geometries, so implementation must handle coefficient jumps and singularities carefully.
paper_title: Wavenumber-explicit stability and preasymptotic error analysis of UPML finite element method for obstacle scattering problems
